stale_plan_conditions: Reverify the three successful repository check names/app15368 within7days before apply. Required names need not have run on main, but candidate PR workflow must actually run all three.
If a branch protection object or ruleset is created meanwhile, PUT protection overwrites whole-object — re-GET and merge into the existing rules instead of applying verbatim.
If the repo becomes private, secret scanning/push protection may need GitHub Advanced Security; a PATCH 403 then is a plan limit, not a payload bug.
If org-level rulesets appear (re-run rulesets?includes_parents=true), org rules may already impose checks; reconcile before adding repo protection.
If the 'receiver' job is renamed, the stale context silently blocks all merges — detect via check-runs on a fresh main SHA.
strict:true presumes no merge queue; if the repo adopts a merge queue, switch to the merge-queue-aware protection fields instead.
post_apply_readback: GET /repos/.../branches/main/protection -> strict true, exactly receiver/runtime-config/ingress-contract from app15368, admins enforced, force pushes/deletions disallowed.
GET /repos/... -> security_and_analysis.secret_scanning.status 'enabled' and secret_scanning_push_protection.status 'enabled' (enablement can be eventual; re-GET once if 'enabling').
GET /repos/.../rulesets?includes_parents=true -> record any ruleset that appeared; reconcile with the protection object.
Enforcement proof still needs one real merge attempt on a PR missing 'receiver' — configuration GETs alone do not prove the gate.
